title: Furnica — learn algorithms with an ant
description: A free program for students: write simple commands and the ant walks across the table, pushing letters until they form a word. For Windows, Linux and macOS.
hero_lead: Students write simple commands — UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT — and the ant walks across the table, pushing the letters in its way until they spell the word. That is how they learn what an algorithm, a loop and a procedure are.
hero_compat: .ant programs from the original Furnica (Ant v2.00, 1999) open and run without any changes.
screenshot_alt: The Furnica window: the program on the left, the table where the ant spelled “conferinta” on the right
f1_title: Set up the table with the mouse
f1_text: Drag the ant to move it, click it to turn it. Type letters straight onto the table, as in a text, and move or erase them with the mouse. The table can be anything from 3 × 3 to 20 × 20 cells.
f2_text: The program is checked on every edit, before it runs: misspelled words, unclosed blocks, missing or unused procedures, loops that never move the ant. For a misspelled word, the Fix button puts in the right one.
f3_text: The ant walks smoothly and its path stays drawn on the table. The editor highlights the line being executed. Run it step by step, pause it, slow it down or finish instantly.
